subject: Checkoutly production latency spike — exec war-room
messages:
From: Rita Gomez <rita.gomez@checkoutly.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@checkoutly.com
Date: 2027-06-16T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Urgent: Checkout latency spike — blocking production

Team,

We started seeing sustained 95th-percentile latency jump on our Checkout route at ~08:30 PDT. Token-level error rate has climbed from ~0.1% to 1.9%, and throughput dropped by ~25% (timeouts and retries). This is impacting live conversions — our guardrails are already flagging a revenue impact.

Attached a quick screenshot from our dashboard (screenshot_latency.png). Key observations:
- Spike aligns with a model rollout at 08:25 (we were auto-updated to redwood-model-v2.1)
- Error payloads show downstream inference timeouts and occasional 500s from the Redwood API
- We have an upcoming Black Friday-style campaign at 09:00; escalation is critical.

Please advise immediate next steps. We need an exec-level bridge and a short list of mitigations we can apply from our side (traffic routing, feature flag toggles) while you investigate.

Rita Gomez
Head of Site Reliability, Checkoutly
rita.gomez@checkoutly.com
+1 415-555-0134

Attachment: screenshot_latency.png (png)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Rita Gomez <rita.gomez@checkoutly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-16T08:50:12-07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: Checkout latency spike — blocking production

Rita — thank you for the quick heads up and the screenshot. We’ve opened an incident (PD-7921) and are spinning up an exec bridge right now. cc’ing our on-call infra and the engineering lead.

Immediate plan (initial):
1) Stand up a triage bridge (10min) — link: https://zoom.us/j/1234567890 (bridge created).
2) Canary rollback to redwood-model-v2.0 for Checkoutly traffic (if agreed) — will reduce risk of regression.
3) Short-term routing: we can route 30% of traffic to a warm Dedicated pool in us-west-2 to reduce burst pressure.
4) Telemetry: David will post a telemetry snapshot and correlation with KV cache behavior.

I’m escalating to our COO for executive visibility; we’ll provide an hourly readout. Attaching a short initial action plan for the bridge and customer comms (initial_action_plan.pdf).

Jonas Weber
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-16T09:08:34-07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: Checkout latency spike — blocking production

Jonas / team — joining bridge now. Quick telemetry summary as I’m seeing it:
- 08:24–08:27: model rollout to redwood-model-v2.1 across hosted tenants (matches customer note)
- 08:28 onwards: KV-cache miss rate spikes on us-west-2 serving nodes for quantized 8-bit runtime; observed memory churn on GPU X500 nodes at ~68% -> GC-related stalls
- Error profile: 70% timeouts (inference step), 30% 500s (internal serving layer)

Proposed immediate mitigations (we can run these in parallel):
A) Traffic canary: route 50% of Checkoutly traffic to redwood-model-v2.0 (safe rollback) for 20 minutes while we observe error rate — requires customer opt-in.
B) Hotfix: bump KV cache window and lower batching to reduce memory pressure; rolling config change across 6 pods (estimated 6–8 minutes to finish).
C) Warm Dedicated route: bring up a Dedicated pool (us-west-2) with pinned v2.0 instances — warm time ~12 minutes but will absorb traffic.

I have a short mitigation runbook attached (mitigation_runbook.md) with exact curl commands and rollback steps. If we approve A+B now we should see error rate fall within 15–20 mins.

I’ll post live telemetry to the Slack incident channel: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C02AXXXXX/ and update PD.

-David

--
David Kim
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-16T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: Checkout latency spike — blocking production

Thanks — joining the bridge now. We approve the Canary rollback (route 50% to v2.0) and will enable routing to Dedicated if error rate does not drop below 1.0% within 20 minutes.

Two asks from our side:
- Please provide hourly updates in this thread and the PD incident.
- If error rate exceeds 2.0% at any point, we will pause customer-facing traffic and notify our product ops.

Appreciate the rapid response.

Rita
